key_evidence_spans: A 37-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, was found on routine blood screening at 10 weeks’ gestation to have pancytopenia
She reported occasional easy bruising over the prior two months but no bleeding, lymphadenopathy, or splenomegaly
Skin biopsy showed dermal neutrophils with upper dermal edema and a subepidermal blister, consistent with bullous Sweet’s syndrome
She was given a presumptive diagnosis of immune thrombocytopenia in pregnancy
Her fatigue persisted but she had no bleeding complications
Five weeks postpartum, she developed a pustular rash on the left upper arm, abdomen, and back
Her blood counts remained low: hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, white-cell count 1.7×10^9/L (neutrophils 0.5×10^9/L, monocytes 0.1×10^9/L), and platelets 49×10^9/L
